summary: Intermittent high p99 inference latency for Nimbus Analytics after transit BGP flap caused cross-region egress redirects
description: Issue summary: Nimbus Analytics reported intermittent spikes in p95/p99 token latencies and occasional streaming disconnects beginning 2026-03-10 09:30 UTC. The traffic from eu-central and ap-south customer routes was unexpectedly egressed via a US region path for short windows, producing increased RTT and retransmits. Impacted requests timed out or observed partial stream chunks (client saw repeated reconnects).
impact: Customer-facing inference latency regression: p99 increased from ~420ms to 2.2s for streaming tokens; ~8% elevated request error rate (stream aborts) for production traffic during windows. Affected customer workflows: interactive analytics dashboards and low-latency assistants; revenue-impacting for dedicated contract SLA.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Use Nimbus Analytics account (dedicated) in eu-central with streaming API for redwood/gpt-6b-fp16. 2) Run steady traffic at ~25 rps with 1–3s prompts. 3) Observe token streaming p50/p95/p99 over 5–15 minute windows. Note: issue reproduced intermittently; correlates with BGP AS path changes visible in routing logs.
logs_and_traces: Sample traces: trace_id=trc-20260310-eu-71a2 (p99 spike at 2026-03-10T09:33:12Z). Edge proxy logs show upstream egress selected: eu-edge -> us-west-egress (unexpected). TCP stats show increased retransmits and dupACKs (tcp_retransmits=11 over 30s window). TLS logs: session resumptions failing for ~3% of streams (TLS_ERR: handshake timeout). See attached packet-capture partials: s3://redwood-support/sup-91527/pcap-20260310-partial.pcap
investigation_notes: Timeline: 2026-03-10 09:30 UTC — customer reports. 09:35 — support validated elevated p99 for eu-central/nimbus. 09:50 — network team observed transient BGP withdrawal from TransitProviderX that caused AS path to shift; our egress selection heuristics briefly preferred a circuit through us-west (longer MPLS hop). 10:10 — forced affinity to local egress for Nimbus account; p99 dropped back to baseline. Hypothesis: TransitProviderX flap induced route redistribution; our egress health weighting algorithm under-weighted path latency when multiple egress options existed, resulting in cross-region egress. Evidence: BGP table change (AS path changed from ...6453,701 to ...6453,1205,701), traceroutes show +180ms RTT after redistribution. Follow-ups: request partner ROA/peering confirmation, add BGP-change alerting to egress selection dashboards.
customer_messages: Customer note (Nimbus): "Since this morning we saw our analytics dashboard lagging and occasional failed streaming responses. Our SLA requires consistent p95 < 1s; this disrupted a live demo. Please update on root cause and mitigation."
comments: 2026-03-10 09:40 — Support (Aisha): Acknowledged, collecting traces and contacting network team.
2026-03-10 09:55 — Network (Diego Morales): Observed BGP withdrawal from TransitProviderX; routing briefly preferred a less optimal egress. Filing with NOC.
2026-03-10 10:15 — Eng (Liam): Applied temporary account-level egress pin for Nimbus to eu-central-edge; monitoring for stabilization.
2026-03-10 11:05 — Support (Aisha): Customer informed of temporary mitigation; asked for permission to keep pinned while root cause investigated.
2026-03-11 14:00 — Network (Diego): TransitProviderX confirmed a partial route flap affecting one POP; suggested BGP dampening tuning on their side.
resolution: Mitigation: temporarily pinned Nimbus Analytics traffic to region-local egress (eu-central or ap-south-1 depending on origin) which restored p99 to baseline. Root cause: transient BGP withdrawal at TransitProviderX combined with egress health-weighting that prioritized available capacity over measured latency, resulting in cross-region egress selection. Permanent fix: 1) roll out egress selection config change to include path RTT as a hard factor for 60s after BGP changes; 2) add BGP-change alerting and automated fallback to last-known-good local egress for dedicated accounts; 3) coordinate with TransitProviderX for route stability improvements. Post-incident: network postmortem scheduled and customer credit discussed.
follow_up_tasks: ENG-2342: add RTT weighting into egress selection (priority)
NET-1187: integrate BGP-change webhook into routing controller
